chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

When the Muhrim (person in Ihram) slaughters the game, neither the Halal (one not in Ihram) nor the Haram (one in Ihram) should eat it, and it is like the dead body (of a non-slaughtered animal). And when the game is slaughtered in the Haram (sanctuary), it is a dead body, whether the one who slaughtered it was Halal or Haram.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game slaughtered by a person in Ihram or within the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of game meat based on the location of slaughter rather than the state of the slaughterer, a key distinction in Shia fiqh. It establishes that hunting within the Haram boundaries renders the meat *Maytah* (dead meat) universally, whereas hunting outside the Haram by an *Muhrim* restricts consumption to those also in Ihram, preserving the sanctity of the ritual state. This ruling underscores the spatial sanctity of the Haram, linking physical boundaries to ritual purity and dietary law.
